planting.note: Set container divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; this hybrid selection (US Plant Patent PP37,175) was bred by Brent Horvath of Intrinsic Perennial Gardens from two Pycnanthemum incanum parents for darker, more colorful foliage.

directions: Smokey Mountain Mint stands out among mountain mints for its smoky gray-purple foliage and silvery, minty-scented growing tips, which stay ornamental from late spring until the white, lavender-flecked flower clusters open in early summer and continue to frost. Plant in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; like other Pycnanthemum it resents constantly wet feet but otherwise asks for little once established, tolerating heat and drought with ease. The dense flower clusters are an exceptional magnet for small native bees, wasps, and beneficial flies, consistently ranking among the top pollinator-support plants in garden trials. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor and control its moderate rhizomatous spread.

common_name: Pinot Noir Foxglove Beardtongue (Deep Red-Black Foliage Native Penstemon)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in average to evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Pinot Noir is a 2025 Intrinsic Perennial Gardens introduction (US Plant Patent PP37,529) bred by Brent Horvath from the cultivar 'Pocahontas' as the female parent.

directions: Pinot Noir carries beet-red to near-black foliage on both leaf surfaces that deepens further in summer heat, bred by Brent Horvath from the cultivar 'Pocahontas' crossed with an unnamed white-flowered selection. In June, stiff 3-to-4-foot stems carry foxglove-like spikes of lavender-pink-and-white tubular flowers that draw bumblebees, mason bees, and hummingbirds; the ornamental seed capsules that follow extend interest into fall. It grows readily in most soils from full sun to light shade and tolerates both heavy clay and brief drought once established. Leave the sturdy winter rosette of glossy dark foliage uncut for extra cold-season structure, then tidy it in early spring before new growth resumes.

common_name: Undaunted Lemon Max Maximilian Sunflower (Native Perennial Sunflower)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in average to lean soil, including heavy clay, in full sun; this garden hybrid was discovered and selected by horticulturist Lauren Springer Ogden in her Fort Collins, Colorado garden, a cross of Helianthus maximiliani with the cultivar 'Lemon Queen'.

directions: Undaunted Lemon Max produces an abundance of large, clear lemon-yellow daisy flowers stacked along sturdy upright stems for several weeks in August, when many other native perennials are winding down for fall. It arose as a chance garden hybrid between Maximilian sunflower and the cultivar 'Lemon Queen,' discovered by horticulturist Lauren Springer Ogden and later introduced through High Country Gardens, combining the species' cold hardiness and tidy, non-running habit with richer flower color. It tolerates clay, drought, and poor soil far better than typical garden sunflowers and needs no staking. Native bees work the nectar-rich flowers heavily through late summer, and goldfinches and other seed-eating birds return through fall and winter if the dried flower heads are left standing.
